children.prompt: Use the bisection method to approximate $\sqrt[3]{2}$ accurate to one decimal place.

answer.short:
$\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.3$ (1 decimal place).

Repeated midpoint tests give $1.25<\sqrt[3]{2}<1.28125$; both endpoints round to $1.3$.
answer.worked:
Since $1^3<2<2^3$, initially $1<\sqrt[3]{2}<2$. Test the midpoint of the current interval each time:
$$\begin{align*}1.5^3&=3.375>2\\1.25^3&=1.953125<2\\1.375^3&=2.599609375>2\\1.3125^3&=2.260986328125>2\\1.28125^3&=2.103302001953125>2.\end{align*}$$
The successive intervals are $(1,1.5)$, $(1.25,1.5)$, $(1.25,1.375)$, $(1.25,1.3125)$ and $(1.25,1.28125)$. Both final endpoints round to $1.3$, so $\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.3$, accurate to one decimal place.
